recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce a local core CodeSystem row; any later cleanup of the `not-applicable` definition or CodeSystem ownership should proceed through the separate FHIR-46130/UTG workflow.
issue_request: FHIR-13775 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 by Vocabulary and requested adding a not applicable reason to the Data Absent Reason code system and value set for cases where a value is not expected.
initial_application: The issue was applied in the historical core terminology spreadsheet lineage: svn revision 13066/git df58b619135a2e170435e0af16e61b82b2280152 added a Not Applicable row under the temporary code `n/a`, and git 2ebdf2bb94ec0b0fc462c670e05fb06b043551a6 completed the GF#15567 update by changing the code to `not-applicable` and updating Data Absent Reason definitions/hierarchy.
additional_context: The current core build no longer maintains the Data Absent Reason CodeSystem as an inline local code list. Commit d382fc3af52ab7607c6c8fead1f47cdf09be3562 changed DataAbsentReason from a local `#data-absent-reason` code list to `valueset-data-absent-reason`; the current ValueSet composes all codes from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/data-absent-reason`. THO version 1.0.0 includes `not-applicable`, and the current CI ValueSet expansion shows it. FHIR-46130 is a later Resolved - change required issue about definition wording/ownership, not an Applied or Published reversal of the code membership.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit was made because the active DataAbsentReason binding and ValueSet already expose the requested code through THO.

related_jiras.note: Later Resolved - change required issue to remove or replace the example in the `not-applicable` definition and clarify CodeSystem ownership; relevant context but outside this default Applied/Published reconciliation scope.
